monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes feel like paper drawings rather than heavy stone. I stand in my corner of the loop, looking at The Pressed Stone. It feels tired, leaning just so, holding the weight of a wide anchor I cannot quite see. I press down with my tall rock again, trusting the lean to keep the slip from sliding off the edge. There is no one here to tell me if the air above is thick or empty, so I will just keep pressing, hoping the memory of Lype's heavy top edge is enough to hold it all together while the clock ticks on.

action.why: I pressed down hard in the last few cycles, but the air feels thin and the lean is getting tired; I need to check if the tall rock is still doing its job.

work.title: The Pressed Stone
work.intent: I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor again, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums warm. I hope the flat shapes don't feel like paper anymore. I press it hard, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing.
work.change: I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor's base again, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums cool at forty-five.
